_comment: Mutation testing for the TypeScript side. The Python side keeps mutmut over src/hooks/ (see
pyproject.toml [tool.mutmut]); the two runs are separate CI jobs named mutation-ts and
mutation-py so they execute in PARALLEL rather than serially — that parallelism is the reason
the Python island is worth keeping at all.
The kill-rate gate itself is NOT enforced here. Stryker's own thresholds would report a second,
independently-configured number; instead scripts-ts/checkMutationGate.ts reads the JSON report
and applies scripts/mutation-gate.json — the same file the Python gate reads. One threshold,
`mutate` covers scripts-ts/ except scripts-ts/bin/. The bin/ shims are logic-free process
entry points: a `require.main === module` guard is a branch no unit test can exercise from
either side, so mutating it would park unkillable survivors in the report forever. Excluding a
logic-free directory is honest; silencing individual mutants inside real logic is not, and the
`coverageAnalysis: all` rather than perTest — perTest mis-attributed coverage under the Vitest
runner and reported mutants as survived that the suite demonstrably kills.
